text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.84% today, recovering slightly after a sharp 3.7% drop on November 18th. The recovery appears tied to geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Saudi Arabia and Bahrain reported new attacks involving Iranian-backed forces and Iranian projectiles—which typically pushes oil prices higher by raising supply concerns. US crude is trading around $89.50 per barrel, though the stock remains well below its November 13th level of $142.28, suggesting the broader market has repriced energy stocks downward over the past week.

Europe's depleted natural gas stocks and the threat of a polar vortex breakdown are adding structural support to energy prices, while long-term demand signals like data center electricity surging by 2030 could sustain higher energy needs. However, today's modest gain masks the fact that ConocoPhillips has lost ground overall in this two-week window, indicating that near-term geopolitical relief hasn't yet fully offset whatever pressures knocked the stock down from $142 earlier this month.
